content: I need to figure out a baking schedule that works with my work schedule. Right now I'm doing the bulk ferment during the day but I keep missing the shaping window because I get pulled into meetings.
A cold retard approach would give you more flexibility. You could mix and do your folds in the evening, let it bulk ferment overnight in the fridge, then shape and bake in the morning before work.

That's what I've been thinking. The fridge slows fermentation enough that I get an 8-12 hour window instead of needing to catch it at exactly the right moment. Same concept as message queues — buffer the work and process it when you're ready.
The cold retard also develops more complex flavors from the slower fermentation. Many bakers prefer it specifically for the flavor profile.

Right, the lactic acid bacteria are more active at lower temperatures relative to the yeast, so you get more tang. I like that. My plan is: mix at 8pm, folds until 10pm, into the fridge overnight, pull at 6am, shape, proof 2 hours, bake at 8am before standup.
That schedule works well. The 2-hour final proof at room temperature after cold retard should be enough for a good oven spring, especially if the bulk went well.
Perfect. Fundamentally this is about designing the process around my constraints rather than fighting them — same thing I tell my team about system design.
